target_customer: Fintechs, exchanges and businesses in Latin America that need to move between stablecoins and local currencies
problem: Access to stablecoin liquidity and FX in Latin America is thin. Rio offers OTC trading and market making between stablecoins and local currencies in Mexico, Colombia, Peru and Brazil.
business_model: Stablecoin FX spread and market making fees (OTC and liquidity provision)

founders.name: Javier Roberts
founders.role: Listed on YC page as Building Rio

founders.name: Ricardo Villarreal Chapa
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Employer names not given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Execution is mostly liquidity sourcing, compliance and settlement rails across several countries. Software is standard, regulatory and counterparty work is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity relationships and licences help, but the service is a trading desk that larger exchanges can replicate. Circle lists Rio as a partner.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bitso later published stablecoin liquidity content for the Brazil and Mexico corridor and Circle connected USDC to local rails in September 2024. No acquisition of Rio found.

market_need_then: Stablecoins such as USDC and USDT were widely used in Latin America for cross border payments and savings. Circle's partner directory lists Rio as an OTC and market making provider in four countries. No 2022 dated demand source was captured.

branding.domain_note: Uses rio.trade rather than rio.com, per the YC listing.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for the brand surfaced unrelated Rio tokens and Ripio. No press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Rio joined YC in Summer 2022 and positions itself as a stablecoin liquidity provider for Latin America, with Circle listing it as a partner. No funding announcement, exit, shutdown or rebrand was found, and one profile says its beta products were pending regulatory approvals, so the outcome is unknown and regulation is the main open risk.
notes: The company website returned HTTP 403 and was not worked around. Funding of about $500K (Caplight June 2022, CB Insights convertible note, Seedtable Sept 2022) appears only on aggregators with conflicting dates, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Competitor search found no sources dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Bitso and Ripio are later or undated mentions. Founding year not found. No outcome events found. Completeness pass: one round of about $500K dated 2022-06 rests on a single database (Caplight, labelled accelerator); CB Insights calls it a convertible note and Seedtable dates a seed to 2022-09, so type and date conflict and no press source exists.
